full_judgment: 4. With regard to the submissions that the order of removal is vitiated on account of failure of the authority to give a notice of proposed punishment, it is seen that Public Servant (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1960 require that the competent authority after enquiry shall give further opportunity to show cause against the proposed punishment. In this connection it may be mentioned that the petitioner's present case is governed under the rules of 1960. It may be further mentioned that although Government Servant (Discipline and Appeals) Rules, 1976 do not provide any specific provision for a second show cause notice proposing any measure of punishment as such but it appears that the Establishment Division of the Government issued an office Memorandum No. RVI/S-37/77-80 dated 8th August, 1977 directing the concerned authorities to issue a second show cause notice before imposition of any major punishment. The authority is required under the rules to communicate to the petitioner the punishment proposed and the report containing {grounds upon which it proposes to impose such punishment. There is nothing on record or in the affidavit-in-opposition that a second show cause notice against the proposed punishment has been given to the petitioner. In this view the failure to give further opportunity to show cause against the proposed punishment under these rules has vitiated the order of removal. In this connection reference may be made to a decision of the High Court Division reported in 30 D.L.R. 144 In that view the order of removal is liable to be set aside. The enquiry that has been concluded shall not however be reopened as such. The petitioner will be entitled only to a further notice to show cause against the proposed punishment. After consideration of his reply, if any, the appointing authority which is competent to dismiss or remove the petitioner shall take such action at it deems fit and proper. The impugned order is set aside and it is declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
